newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs eye upside, but auction may weigh.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs eye upside, but auction may weigh.

text.p: European bond markets again reversed early U.S.-inspired weakness to trade firmer on Thursday but Belgian dealers said any gains in OLOs could be capped because of new supply due Monday.

Around 0800 GMT the benchmark 10-year, 6.25 pct OLO 26 maturing March 2007 was yielding 5.76 percent, unchanged on Wednesday's close despite initially rising slightly because of overnight weakness in U.S. Treasuries.
However, the Belgian market lagged slightly Germany, with the 10-year spread edging out to nine from eight basis points and dealers said this could be because of the upcoming auction.
The 10-year benchmark is being sold alongside OLO 10, the benchmark five-year 8.75 pct maturing June 2002.
Dealers said the Treasury had told primary dealers earlier this week that talk of a new 10-year benchmark being issued was premature and no decision would be taken for at least two months.

One trader said, however, he was still optimistic that the Treasury would take the plunge, probably launching a 10-year with a February 2008 maturity. "It would suit the Treasury to have a benchmark with a coupon which was closer to market yields," he said.
